clue.text: Policeman at seaside reported a tree

parts.note: a copper is British slang for a police officer

indicators.note: reported means the word for the seaside is given as it would be spoken

parts.note: the seaside is the beach

explanation.surface: A constable on duty at the seaside files a report about a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link word; the seaside word BEACH is said aloud and gives the tree's spelling instead.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a variety of the European tree with dark reddish-purple leaves, often planted in parks.

clue.text: Poem about universal Balkan currency in action before 19 in 18

indicators.note: about means the poem's letters go around the next pieces

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal
the denar is the currency of North Macedonia, a Balkan state

explanation.surface: A poem about a Balkan currency seems tied to some earlier military campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 in 18 is PLAQUE inside MALT, giving MALPLAQUET (1709); Marlborough fought this battle in 1708, just before it. The theme is his four great victories.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1708 battle in Flanders was the Duke of Marlborough's victory immediately preceding his fight at Malplaquet in 1709.

clue.text: Original border circumvented by friend

indicators.note: circumvented by means the friend word goes right round the border word

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: An original boundary is walked around by a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Primal means first or earliest, the same sense as original in 'original sin'.

clue.text: One who paints modern girls in action before 2

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword painter
Millies, from the musical Thoroughly Modern Millie

explanation.surface: A painter of fashionable young women seems to have seen earlier service.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts. 'Modern girls' alludes to the musical Thoroughly Modern Millie. Ramillies (1706) came before Oudenarde (1708).
explanation.definitionFit: This 1706 battle was Marlborough's victory fought two years before his battle at Oudenarde, the solution at 2.

clue.text: Singer found only in wood and water

parts.note: just means only, as in 'just a minute'
timber is wood
a lake is a body of water

explanation.surface: A singer is discovered only out in the woods and the water.
explanation.definitionFit: An American pop singer, formerly of the boy band NSYNC, known for solo hits.

clue.text: Cream of jest — affair's not Irish but Orange

indicators.note: the cream is the top of the milk, so the cream of jest is its leading letter
not means the Irish abbreviation is taken out of the word affair

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive adding nothing

explanation.surface: A joke about a romance that is Orange rather than Irish, hinting at Ulster politics.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on Orange as the Ulster Protestant tradition opposed to Irish nationalism; the definition is the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaffa is a familiar variety of sweet thick-skinned orange, named after the port near Tel Aviv.

clue.text: See Arthur about his father — Irish, not Orange?

indicators.note: about means the son word goes around the father's name

parts.note: Arthur, seen in relation to his father, is a son
King Arthur's father was Uther Pendragon

explanation.surface: Ask about King Arthur's father, and whether he was Irish or an Orangeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link telling you to view Arthur from his father's side, as a son. Southern Irish people are contrasted with Orangemen, the Protestant loyalists concentrated in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Southern Irish suggests the Catholic South of Ireland, in contrast to the Orange, loyalist tradition of the North.

clue.text: Lower international organisation — I must be joking

parts.note: INF is the abbreviation of inferior or infra, meaning lower or below
the UN is the United Nations

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a junior world body, insisting they don't mean it.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something just for a laugh is the idiom for not being serious, as 'I must be joking' admits.

clue.text: Anarchic movement puts barrier round platform

indicators.note: round means the barrier word encloses the platform word

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across water
a dais is a raised platform

explanation.surface: An unruly protest group erects a fence round the speaker's stage.
explanation.definitionFit: This early twentieth-century art movement rejected logic and convention, so anarchic describes it well.

clue.text: Paid the wrong bill to send off a sub?

definitions.text: Paid the wrong bill to send off a sub?

parts.words: Paid the wrong bill to send off a sub?
parts.note: a debt charge is a bill; the near-sounding naval weapon is what you pay out to dispose of a submarine, so the wrong bill is paid

explanation.surface: Someone settled the wrong invoice when dispatching a subscription or deputy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sub' looks like a subscription or substitute, and 'send off' like posting or dismissing; it is a submarine being destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: This underwater explosive is dropped from ships to destroy submarines, the 'sub' of the clue.

clue.text: Made a mistake and got softened up?

definitions.meaning: to make a hash of a line or a catch
made fluffy, like a pillow plumped and softened

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both botched, as an actor botches a line, and made soft and fluffy.

clue.text: I don't agree to delete another two insets

annotationWithheld.why: I don't agree to delete another two insets (11): 'I don't agree' defines DISSENTIENT, but no parse found for 'to delete another two insets' giving the letters
annotationWithheld.clue: I don't agree to delete another two insets

clue.text: They have openings for speculators — note: everything's at the speed of sound among the trees

indicators.note: among means the following pieces sit inside the trees word

parts.note: pines are trees
NB, nota bene, means note well
all is everything
Mach one, written MACH I, is the speed of sound

explanation.surface: A tip for investors about everything moving at supersonic speed in the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is a link. The speculators are gamblers putting coins into slots, not investors.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcade games have coin slots for players who gamble a coin on scoring, hence openings for speculators.

clue.text: The one who wins the girl's love?

definitions.text: The one who wins the girl's love?

parts.words: The one who wins the girl's love?
parts.note: the leading man of a romance wins the girl; also, in Greek legend, Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to the priestess he loved, so the girl herself is meant

explanation.definitionFit: The leading man of a romance is the one who gets the girl; Leander's beloved priestess also bore this name.

clue.text: See 5
Battle by lake with cold and hot material

parts.note: Bala Lake is the largest natural lake in Wales
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
lava is molten rock

explanation.surface: A battle fought beside a lake in conditions both freezing and scorching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' and 'with' are link words. Balaclava, also a woollen helmet, was the 1854 Crimean battle of the Charge of the Light Brigade.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1854 Crimean War engagement included the Charge of the Light Brigade.

clue.text: Knowledge of a missing Trojan 12 about battles

annotationWithheld.why: Knowledge of a missing Trojan 12 about battles (9): AWARENESS needs A + WAR(ENES)S, but AENEAS less one A gives ENEAS or AENES, not ENES, without 'a' doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Knowledge of a missing Trojan 12 about battles

clue.text: Apple in action before 4

definitions.meaning: the ... Orange is an old English apple variety
a battle fought earlier than the one at 4

explanation.walkthrough: Blenheim (1704) preceded Ramillies (1706), the solution at 4.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both an English dessert apple variety and Marlborough's 1704 victory in Bavaria.

clue.text: Shelley's editor edited without thinking

indicators.note: edited means the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, including the S

explanation.surface: An editor revised the poet Shelley's work carelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without thinking is acting carelessly, without paying attention.

clue.text: Whisky for beer

definitions.meaning: single ... is a type of whisky
germinated barley used for brewing beer

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a whisky made from malted barley and the grain prepared for brewing.

clue.text: Floss wanted memorial tablet

definitions.meaning: dental floss is wanted to remove the film on teeth
a commemorative plate fixed to a wall

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the film on teeth that floss removes and a commemorative wall tablet.

clue.text: Birds get on with old king that's admitted member of Cambridge body

parts.note: robins are birds

indicators.note: admitted means the member is let into the king's name

parts.note: Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme
a leg is a limb or member

explanation.surface: Some birds join an ancient king who lets in a member of a Cambridge institution.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the constituent colleges of Cambridge University, founded in 1979.

clue.text: See 1
Polar 12's report of grain

indicators.note: report of means the grain word is given as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: oats are a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A polar explorer's account of the cereal supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is a link. Captain Oates walked out to his death on Scott's 1912 Antarctic expedition to save his comrades, a celebrated act of heroism.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawrence Oates was a hero of Scott's polar expedition, famous for walking out into the blizzard.

clue.text: The day before the Sabbath is a high point

parts.note: the eve is the day before an event
the Sabbath is the day of rest

explanation.surface: Saturday is the peak of the week, just ahead of the Sabbath.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan mountain is the world's highest peak, literally the highest point on earth.

clue.text: French boy losing his head: time for something he's got?

indicators.note: losing his head means the first letter of the name goes

parts.note: Jacques is a French boy's name

explanation.surface: A French lad loses his temper: about time, given what he's acquired.
explanation.definitionFit: An acquest is a legal term for property acquired, something gained rather than inherited.

clue.text: Flower could be the same when cut

indicators.note: could be means the letters may be rearranged into something else
cut means the phrase is docked of its last letter

explanation.surface: A flower might look identical once trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cut' docks THE SAME to THESAM, and 'could be' rearranges those letters. A flower here is a river, something that flows: the one through London.
explanation.definitionFit: In crosswords a flower is a river, something that flows, and this is London's river.

clue.text: A line that isn't in favour

parts.note: a verse is a line of poetry

explanation.surface: A line of text that expresses opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opposed or disinclined to something means not being in favour of it.
